name: scholarship-election-bill
computation: Pub. 970 chapter 2 Example 3 (Bill) with 2026 amounts. Single filer, born 1998-03-01 (age 28), the American opportunity credit student: Form 1098-T box 1 $5,600.00 and box 5 $5,600.00 (a grant that may pay room and board), living costs paid $4,400.00, the part of the grant included in income chosen by the App. One W-2: box 1 $39,250.00, box 2 $3,000.00. Parts tried (adjusted qualified expenses = $5,600 - ($5,600 - X)): X = $0 gives taxable income $23,150 (row midpoint $23,175: $1,240 + 12% x $10,775 = $2,533) and no credit, net $2,533; X = $2,000 gives $25,150 ($2,773) less a $2,000 credit = $773; X = $4,000 gives $27,150 (row midpoint $27,175: $1,240 + 12% x $14,775 = $3,013) less a $2,500 credit ($2,000 + 25% x $2,000) = $513; X = $4,400 gives $27,550 ($3,061) less the same $2,500 = $561. The App keeps $4,000. Schedule 1 line 8r $4,000.00 -> Form 1040 line 8 $4,000.00; line 9 = $39,250.00 + $4,000.00 = $43,250.00; line 11 AGI $43,250.00; line 12e $16,100.00; line 15 = $27,150.00; line 16 = $3,013.00. The credit is $2,500: 40% = $1,000 refundable (line 29; the filer is 28), $1,500 nonrefundable (Schedule 3 line 3). Line 24 total tax = $3,013.00 - $1,500.00 = $1,513.00. Line 25a $3,000.00; line 33 = $3,000 + $1,000 = $4,000.00; line 34 = $4,000.00 - $1,513.00 = $2,487.00.
